definitions.explanation: A legal term meaning a crime that has been fully carried out, with all elements of the offense completed. Contrasted with {未遂|みすい} (attempted but not completed). Used in criminal law, court judgments, and news reporting on criminal cases.

examples.japanese: {詐欺|さぎ}{既遂|きすい}の{罪|つみ}で{起訴|きそ}された。
examples.english: He was indicted on a charge of consummated fraud.

examples.japanese: {既遂|きすい}か{未遂|みすい}かで{刑|けい}の{重|おも}さが{大|おお}きく{変|か}わる。
examples.english: Whether the crime was consummated or merely attempted greatly changes the severity of the sentence.

examples.japanese: {裁判所|さいばんしょ}は{被告|ひこく}の{行為|こうい}を{強盗|ごうとう}{既遂|きすい}と{認定|にんてい}し、{懲役|ちょうえき}{十年|じゅうねん}を{言|い}い{渡|わた}した。
examples.english: The court found the defendant's act to be consummated robbery and sentenced him to ten years in prison.

notes:
Composed of {既|き} (already) and {遂|すい} (to accomplish; to carry through). Literally "already accomplished," contrasted with {未遂|みすい} "not yet accomplished."

USAGE:
A specialized legal term. Most commonly appears attached to the name of a specific crime: {殺人|さつじん}{既遂|きすい} (consummated murder), {強盗|ごうとう}{既遂|きすい} (consummated robbery), {詐欺|さぎ}{既遂|きすい} (consummated fraud). Virtually never used outside legal and crime-reporting contexts. The distinction {既遂|きすい} vs. {未遂|みすい} is important because Japanese criminal law allows lighter sentences for attempted crimes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {殺人|さつじん}{既遂|きすい}: consummated murder
- {既遂|きすい}の{罪|つみ}: the crime of a consummated offense
- {既遂|きすい}と{認定|にんてい}する: to determine (a crime) to be consummated
- {既遂|きすい}{犯|はん}: perpetrator of a consummated crime

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {未遂|みすい}: attempted (but not completed) — the direct antonym, used when the perpetrator fails to complete the crime
- {予備|よび}: preparation (of a crime) — an even earlier stage, punishable only for certain serious offenses
- {実行|じっこう}: execution; carrying out — the general act of committing, not specifically the completed state
